questions.qtext: Which of the following statements are not true about the power consumption in a CMOS NAND gate?

options.text: Dynamic power consumption occurs due to the charging and discharging of load capacitances during switching.
Static power consumption is ideally non-zero when the output is low.
The total power consumption of a CMOS NAND gate depends on the frequency of switching.
Leakage current contributes to the static power consumption, though it is very small in ideal conditions.

questions.solution:
(b)
• Dynamic power is indeed consumed due to the charging and discharging of capacitances when switching states.
• The total power consumption in a CMOS gate depends on the switching frequency because dynamic power is proportional to the switching rate.
• There is a small amount of leakage current even in the steady state, which contributes to static power consumption, though it is ideally minimized in CMOS design.
• Static power consumption is ideally zero in CMOS gates, even when the output is low, because there exists no direct current path from VDD to ground in steady state.

questions.qtext: In a p-n junction diode at equilibrium, which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: The hole and electron drift current components are in same direction.
The hole and electron diffusion current components are in the same direction.
On an average, holes and electrons drift in opposite direction.
On an average, electrons drift and diffuse in the same direction.

questions.solution:
(a, b, c)
In a p-n junction diode, due to the diffusion of charge carriers i.e. electrons from n side to p-side and holes from p-side to n-side, the depletion region is formed and an electric field is set up; due to which electrons on the n-side move away from the junction. Thus, electrons drift and diffuse in the opposite direction. Hence, option (d) is incorrect.
